subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw accept core, default-off SOUL.md auto-evolution, or keep durable preference capture in memory/plugin surfaces instead?
rationale: The request is concrete and current main lacks it, but it adds model-mediated writes to a prompt-loaded instruction file plus new config and CLI surfaces, which repository policy treats as product and security-boundary decisions.

options.title: Accept guarded core contract
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after it uses a private capability, obeys delivery policy, provides visible notice/undo/provenance, and covers hostile input.

options.title: Move to memory or plugin seam
options.body: Reject direct SOUL.md mutation in core and ask for durable preference capture through memory plugins or a new plugin/API extension.

options.title: Decline automatic mutation
options.body: Close the overlapping SOUL auto-evolution requests if maintainers do not want model-mediated instruction-file writes at all.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded core contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after it uses a private capability, obeys delivery policy, provides visible notice/undo/provenance, and covers hostile input.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans SOUL docs, prompt assembly, core-vs-plugin ownership, and security posture, and Peter Steinberger is the strongest feature-history owner in the inspected path.
